title: Cancelling and waiting on a Future

questions.stem: Per this page, a running task never checks for interruption, and its Future receives `cancel(true)`. Which of these then holds?

options.text: isDone() returns false until the task body finishes running
options.says: The page says that after cancellation, regardless of the flag, isDone() returns true, even though a task that ignores interrupts continues running.

options.text: isDone() returns true while the task body is still running
options.says: The page says a task that ignores interrupts will continue running even after cancel(true), and that after cancellation isDone() returns true.

options.text: isCancelled() returns false because the task body kept running
options.says: The page says the Future will report such a task as cancelled: after cancellation isCancelled() returns true.

questions.stem: Per this page, what do virtual threads change about a thread that waits in `Future.get()`?

options.text: The wait is cheaper, since such a thread is inexpensive to park and resume
options.says: The page says blocking on Future.get() is much less costly with virtual threads because they are cheap to park and resume.

options.text: The wait is shorter, since get() on such a thread returns without blocking
options.says: The page still calls Future.get() a blocking call that blocks until the result is available; virtual threads only make that blocking cheaper.

options.text: The wait is rejected, since such a thread is not allowed to block on get()
options.says: The page speaks of blocking on Future.get() from a virtual thread as allowed and cheaper, reducing the need for non-blocking patterns.
